rationale: A wins because it does the adult work: it keeps the launch peg honest and turns the missing customer name into tension instead of wallpaper. Its line "flies power lines with nobody at the controls — and no named utility willing to say so" is reporter-shaped, even if "willing" overreaches. B has useful structure, but "Power-line and substation inspection is dangerous, manual, and expensive work utilities have wanted to automate for years" smuggles in a market brief the update did not supply.
gaps_in_A: "will pay a premium" is unsupported. The update says US-made and positioned against Chinese makers facing import restrictions; it says nothing about price or willingness to pay more.
"no named utility willing to say so" overstates the fact. The release discloses no named utility; it does not prove utilities refused to be named.
"the first concrete evidence of where the 2024 exit led" is too confident. The update says Skydio exited consumers two years ago, not that this is the first proof point since then.
A buries a viable regulatory angle in proof/questions instead of keeping it as its own angle. "What does 'no pilot' mean in regulatory terms?" is a real reporter lane.
gaps_in_B: "Autonomous drones start patrolling America's power grid" implies live national deployment. The update gives a launch and claimed contracts, not active patrols across America.
"dangerous, manual, and expensive work utilities have wanted to automate for years" may be true, but it is not in the update. That is imported context, not grounded angle work.
"a live, contracted enterprise product" and "the clearest evidence yet" both overclaim. Contracts are mentioned; live deployments and comparative company history are not.
"the restrictions themselves are already in effect" asserts legal status the update does not specify. B should have treated that as proof needed, not background fact.
